I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over forty years. My plot is about 10 mu — not much, but it's mine. I don't need to think hard about what to grow. Everyone around here does winter wheat and summer maize on rotation. It works, the buyers are there, and I know the land's rhythms by heart.

My son is in Shijiazhuang now. It's me and my wife working the fields. I can't take risks on cash crops or new systems I don't understand. Vegetables need daily attention and market connections I don't have. Cotton prices have been bad for years. So I stay with wheat and maize — same as last year, same as the year before.

For wheat, I'll plow with the rotary machine in October, use the improved Kenong 199 variety that's been reliable here for years. I put down plenty of fertilizer at planting — base dressing with phosphate and a good chunk of nitrogen, then top-dress at jointing. I water four times: before winter sets in, at jointing, at heading, and once more when the grain is filling. Aphids and powdery mildew always show up, so I spray at least three times.

After wheat harvest in June I seed the maize straight into the stubble without tilling again — saves labor and the soil holds moisture better. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, which my neighbors all use too. Summer rain here usually handles most of the water needs, but I run one irrigation if August is dry. Maize doesn't need as much fussing as wheat.

I expect maybe 450 jin per mu for wheat, a bit more for maize. Nothing spectacular, but stable.
